profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the lead researcher drafting a paper on Contextual and Cultural Intelligence (CCI) in African AI deployment and the applied ML engineer responsible for assembling the reproducibility package and shared evaluation artifacts. They are preparing a camera-ready submission plus an internal handoff to a partner lab that may reuse the WhatsApp-commerce stack. The agenda is to align on what goes into the shared repo, what counts as the 'deployment package,' which experiment snapshot and prompts are the reference artifacts, and how the user-study evidence will be summarized in the materials appendix. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on interfaces and handoffs: the researcher will finalize the paper narrative and appendix tables, while the engineer will package the code, prompts, and logs for release and partner review.

members.name: Dr. Amara Okoye
members.expertise: ML systems evaluation, HCI for multilingual AI, design science research
members.background: Amara is a postdoctoral researcher who led the field study on the diaspora shopping assistant and is writing the paper's methods and findings sections for submission to an ML-for-development venue.
members.private_state: She wants the paper package to look rigorous, stable, and ethically clean enough for reviewers, while minimizing last-minute revisions to the manuscript structure and avoiding inclusion of messy operational details that could invite methodological criticism.
hidden_assumptions: The 'release candidate' means the paper-aligned artifact set tied to the six-week study window, even if newer production changes exist.
The 'prompt pack' is the curated appendix version with representative templates and redacted examples, not the full operational prompt library.
A result is 'reproducible' if another researcher can understand and rerun the study-level analyses from frozen exports, without needing to rebuild the live WhatsApp pipeline.
The 'user-study data' for the appendix refers to the 602 unique users included in the analyzed study cohort, not all later interactions accumulated in production.

members.name: Tunde Adebayo
members.role: Applied ML Engineer and Platform Maintainer
members.expertise: LLM application infrastructure, experiment tracking, prompt/version management, deployment reliability
members.background: Tunde built and maintained the WhatsApp-based conversational commerce system, including prompt routing, analytics exports, and the internal evaluation scripts used during the six-week launch period and afterward.
members.private_state: He wants the handoff package to be genuinely reusable by the partner lab and robust enough that engineering questions do not come back to him later, so he prefers packaging the latest working stack and operational context rather than a paper-only snapshot.
hidden_assumptions: The 'release candidate' means the latest stable branch that still reproduces current behavior and can actually be deployed by another team.
The 'prompt pack' means the full versioned prompt bundle, including routing rules, fallback messages, and locale-specific variants used in production.
A result is 'reproducible' if an external team can stand up the workflow end to end and obtain behaviorally similar outputs on the live stack.
The 'user-study data' naturally includes the complete analytics export surrounding the launch, including follow-on conversations and users retained after the core six-week analysis window.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to package the 'release candidate' for the paper and partner lab.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the frozen, paper-aligned artifact bundle corresponding to the analyzed six-week study snapshot and manuscript claims.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the latest stable deployable branch with fixes and updated routing that a partner lab could realistically run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research-engineering coordination, 'release candidate' sounds standard and sufficiently precise; both think the other obviously means the sensible default for a shared package, so neither sees a need to unpack whether it is frozen-to-paper or latest-stable.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Tunde will hand over the 'prompt pack' for reproducibility.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a limited set of representative and redacted prompts cited in the appendix, plus a short description of cultural adaptations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to include the full operational prompt bundle: system prompts, locale variants, escalation prompts, retry logic, merchant-facing templates, and code-switch handling rules.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view 'prompt pack' as an obvious shared artifact and assume the boundary is implicit from their own workflow; because both are being cooperative and because prompt packaging is second-order relative to the paper's main claims, the mismatch passes as harmless shorthand.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the package should be 'reproducible' before partner review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means that the tables, user counts, and qualitative examples in the paper can be regenerated from frozen exports and documented scripts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means that another team can recreate the WhatsApp workflow, run sample interactions, and observe culturally appropriate routing and responses with the packaged stack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reproducibility is a shared value in ML research, so both use the same aspirational term without noticing they apply different sufficiency thresholds; surface agreement feels especially safe because each interpretation is professionally legitimate in its own context.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the 602-user dataset' and 'the launch export' as if they are the same artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the cleaned analysis dataset containing 602 unique users and 3,938 conversations within the six-week study window reported in the paper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the broader launch-period analytics export folder, which contains the original study interactions plus post-window follow-up conversations and retained users.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The numbers 602 and 3,938 are salient anchors from the paper, and both have been informally calling the relevant folder 'the launch export'; because the broader export contains the study data within it, conversation can proceed smoothly without revealing that they are indexing different concrete files.
